title: Georgy Porgy
year_note: On Toto (10 October 1978); the single came out on 3 April 1979.

notes.made: David Paich wrote it. Steve Lukather sings the verses and plays guitar, Paich piano, Steve Porcaro synths, David Hungate bass and Jeff Porcaro drums, with Lenny Castro on percussion, Jim Horn on sax and flute and Chuck Findley on trumpet; Marty Paich and Sid Sharp arranged the strings. Cheryl Lynn sings the chorus, a twist on the nursery rhyme. The album took nine months, October 1977 to June 1978, at Studio 55 with extra work at Davlen and Sunset Sound.
notes.context: Toto were the session crowd turned band: Paich and Jeff Porcaro had played on Boz Scaggs's Silk Degrees, and the others came from the same circuit. The debut reached 9 on the album chart on the back of 'Hold the Line'. 'Georgy Porgy' stalled at 48 on the Hot 100 but reached 18 on the R&B chart, and hip-hop found it: MC Lyte built 'Poor Georgie' on it in 1991, Eric Benét and Faith Evans remade it in 1999, and Jeezy sampled it in 2011.

listen_for.note: Cheryl Lynn singing the nursery-rhyme line, a big part of why it went to 18 on the R&B chart.

listen_for.where: the groove from the first bar
listen_for.note: Jeff Porcaro's laid-back pocket, which Wikipedia credits to his study of Paul Humphrey, Earl Palmer, Ed Greene and James Gadson.
Lukather singing lead, not Bobby Kimball, which is why it sounds softer than the rest of the debut.

leads_to.title: Poor Georgie
leads_to.why: Built on Georgy Porgy's music, it went to No. 1 on the Hot Rap Singles chart.

notes.unverified: Panel line says 'barely charted'; it did reach 48 pop and 18 R&B.

culture.title: No. 48 pop, No. 18 R&B
culture.line: Released on 3 April 1979, it reached only 48 on the Hot 100 but 18 on the R&B chart.

culture.title: MC Lyte, 'Poor Georgie'
culture.line: MC Lyte's 'Poor Georgie' (December 1991) is built on it and went to No. 1 on the Hot Rap Singles chart.

culture.title: Eric Benét and Faith Evans
culture.line: Eric Benét and Faith Evans remade it in 1999; it reached 2 in New Zealand and 28 in the UK.

culture.title: Jeezy, 'Shake Life'
culture.line: Jeezy sampled it on 'Shake Life' in 2011.
